title: Effort Counts Twice
coreMove: Break achievement into skill-building effort and skill-using effort before judging outcomes.
sourcePressure: Show why effort both builds skill and turns skill into achievement.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing the formula to work harder and ignoring the two separate jobs effort performs.

sourceAnchors.name: Dan Chambliss swimmer study
sourceAnchors.detail: Chambliss spent six years studying competitive swimmers and argued excellence came from many small habits made reliable.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Chambliss watched the miracle dissolve into flip turns, starts, breath timing, and ordinary habits done unusually well.

sourceAnchors.name: Marty Seligman
sourceAnchors.detail: Duckworth recalls Seligman telling her she had data but no theory, which pushed her toward the effort-counts-twice model.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The hard comment from Seligman forced the missing mechanism onto the table.
